strict_validation: passed: both diagnostic builds and five full-process candidate builds
candidate: Read/parse already-prepared canonical source-manifest.json within each timed build; use only Git modes. PDM metadata, selection, generated pyproject and PKG-INFO remain freshly generated. No payload/file-list reuse. Original prototype.py and original evidence.json untouched.
measurement_scope: Only two untimed diagnostic builds include substage instrumentation; five measured builds have diagnostic=False and empty diagnostic_stages. Full-process timer includes worker launch/imports and complete sdist -> full native extraction -> PDM wheel-from-extracted-sdist. No selective extraction. Strict validators are outside timing.
writer_bottleneck: Fresh JSON diagnostic: native gzip writer 0.536s, path.stat/resolve/mtree generation 0.236s, PDM collect+validation 0.139s. Archive permission parsing costs 0.085s versus JSON 0.0043s. Untimed controls: uncompressed native tar 0.457s, gzip level 1 0.467s, --version process 0.021s. Thus compression is not the dominant cost: mtree parsing, source stat/open/read, tar serialization, process/pipe transport dominate native-writer cost collectively. Single controls do not isolate each individual filesystem/serialization cost. No claim that all 0.457s is IO.

node_proposal.available: Existing C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe v24.21.0, process.arch arm64, bundled zlib 1.3.2.1-motley-8002e91; no installs required.
node_proposal.feasible: Builtin fs/promises + zlib.createGzip can replace the native subprocess/mtree stage as an alternative Node child, consuming a freshly PDM-generated per-build map of member names, canonical Git modes and fresh metadata paths. Bound concurrent reads; retain sorted member emission and backpressure. Do not retain source payloads/file selections between builds.
node_proposal.missing_builtin: Node has no builtin tar writer. Need audited USTAR/PAX header/checksum/padding handling, long UTF-8 paths, reproducible metadata, sizes/races and error cleanup. A production-quality generic implementation plus strict mode/RECORD tests exceeds ~200-line disposable scope; proposal only.
node_proposal.benefit_limits: Could avoid Python stat/resolve/mtree overhead and exploit bounded concurrent reads; Node startup still exists. gzip is already native in current tar, so switching zlib alone unlikely to materially change results. Filesystem overhead/concurrency gains unmeasured; do not promise .730s. Extraction belongs to Worker1 and is unchanged here.

confidence.high: 3390 exact canonical Git mode values equal; both diagnostics and all five candidate builds strict-Mac equivalent, including executable scripts and wheel RECORD.
confidence.medium: Small diagnostic samples and five unpaired warm process trials: measured modest improvement, not controlled causal end-to-end attribution. Writer controls support non-compression bottleneck at aggregate level.
confidence.low: Projected Node concurrency benefit: no Node serializer implemented or benchmarked.

housekeeping: Inherited scoped .gitignore excludes source/, **/extracted/, caches/environments, *.whl/*.tar/*.tar.gz. Scripts/JSON/logs visible. Original evidence retained. No CI, tool installations, production/shared source or configuration changes.
